title: Authority, Capability, Permission and Control
results: Ability, Permission, Authority and Control are distinct relations.
Authentication establishes identity/security claims while Authorization evaluates whether concrete access may proceed.
Principal is an authorization/accountability namespace identity rather than necessarily Human Actor, Intender or Executor.
Ordinary capability, Linux privilege capability and object-capability authority are distinct meanings.
Effective privilege/authority differs from potential, inherited and ambient authority.
Explicit capability-like authority can narrow object/action scope and reduce ambient namespace authority.
Bearer credential possession can confer exercisable authority without establishing semantic authorship.
Delegation and attenuation move/narrow authority without requiring identity or Goal-ownership transfer.
Same principal/user identity can execute under different effective authority contexts.
Current Ordivon principal is server-bound Runtime request/idempotency/audit attribution, not a generic authenticated OS/end-user identity.
Current MCP authentication source is distinct from current configured Runtime principal and Bearers are broad single-owner surface gates.
trusted_local and contained_local are effective execution-authority profiles; contained_local is attenuation rather than hostile-code isolation.
Windows limited/elevated is explicit effective execution-authority selection and materially participates in operation identity.
InputAuthority is an operator-owned explicit namespace-authority mechanism; its name, ForeignReferences and HostDependencies are not credentials.
Runtime admission, OS execution and external provider authorization are independent enforcement layers.
Process-tree control/cancellation does not grant external Effect rollback authority.
Revocation/current authorization and historical authority commitments are temporally distinct.
Least authority should minimize unnecessary ambient power while retaining sufficient execution, observation and recovery authority.

nextRound.title: Boundary, Environment, Context and Dependency
nextRound.entryQuestion: Which boundaries and environmental/dependency facts define where an Operation is realized, what Runtime actually owns, and what must be frozen, witnessed, materialized or left open?

notes: RF6 explains current principal/authentication/execution-authority layers but does not authorize new RBAC/capability-token protocols, bearer changes, field renames or execution-profile changes.
